name: Correlation — Possible BEC / Cloud-Account Compromise with Sensitive Data Loss
description:
Attacker objective
Compromise a cloud identity (business email compromise) and use it to exfiltrate sensitive data — the same user shows a suspicious Microsoft 365 identity/mail action (external forwarding, delegation, OAuth consent, app-credential or privileged-role addition) and a DLP exfiltration event.

Attack logic
A suspicious M365 identity or mailbox action is a cloud-account-compromise signal; a DLP incident by the same user is a data-loss signal. Together on one identity they indicate account takeover followed by data theft.

Why this detection works
Correlating an M365 identity/mail alert and a DLP alert on the same normalized user confirms cloud-account compromise with data loss across two domains. The user is normalized to a canonical form and records that cannot be confidently normalized are excluded.

False positives
A power user whose legitimate M365 administration coincides with a routine DLP event.

Tuning
Endpoint DLP user attribution is partial (many records carry a display name rather than a domain login), so this rule is conservative by design and is disabled until user normalization is improved. Enable once the DLP source emits a consistent domain login.

Required telemetry
M365/Entra identity alerts and DLP alerts, joined on the normalized user (canonical lowercased login). NOTE: Forcepoint user attribution is partial — display-name records are excluded from the join.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. norm_user = the identity flagged by both M365 and DLP; review m365_detections and dlp_detections.
2. Treat as possible BEC/account takeover with data loss — reset the account, revoke tokens/app grants, and review the data moved.
3. Because DLP user attribution is partial, absence of a match does not rule out BEC; corroborate with host-based correlation.
false_positives: A power user whose legitimate M365 administration coincides with a routine DLP event.
query:
FROM .alerts-security.alerts-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE kibana.alert.rule.name IN ("Entra ID — Application Credential (Secret or Certificate) Added", "Entra ID — Member Added to a Privileged Directory Role", "Entra ID — OAuth Consent, Permission Grant or Service Principal Added", "Exchange Online — Mailbox External Forwarding Configured", "Exchange Online — Mailbox FullAccess or SendAs Delegation Granted", "SharePoint/OneDrive — Burst of Anonymous Sharing Links by a User", "Exchange Online — Transport (Mail Flow) Rule Created or Modified", "SharePoint — Site Collection Administrator Added", "Microsoft Teams — Application Installed", "Forcepoint DLP — Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public Email by One User", "Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Transfer Outside Working Hours", "Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Sent to a Personal / Public Email Domain", "Forcepoint DLP — Cardholder / PCI Data Transfer")
| EVAL norm_user = TO_LOWER(user.name)
| WHERE norm_user IS NOT NULL AND norm_user != ""
| EVAL is_dlp = kibana.alert.rule.name IN ("Forcepoint DLP — Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public Email by One User", "Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Transfer Outside Working Hours", "Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Sent to a Personal / Public Email Domain", "Forcepoint DLP — Cardholder / PCI Data Transfer")
| STATS m365_alerts = COUNT(CASE(NOT is_dlp, kibana.alert.rule.name, null)), dlp_alerts = COUNT(CASE(is_dlp, kibana.alert.rule.name, null)), m365_detections = VALUES(CASE(NOT is_dlp, kibana.alert.rule.name, null)), dlp_detections = VALUES(CASE(is_dlp, kibana.alert.rule.name, null)), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY norm_user
| WHERE m365_alerts >= 1 AND dlp_alerts >= 1
